subject: math
content: A linear equation is an equation where the variable appears only to the first power, e.g. 2x + 3 = 11. To solve one: (1) simplify both sides, (2) move variable terms to one side and constants to the other using inverse operations, (3) isolate the variable by dividing by its coefficient. Always do the same operation to both sides to keep the equation balanced.

subject: math
content: For a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c: a^2 + b^2 = c^2. It only applies to right triangles. To find a missing side, substitute the two known values, isolate the unknown, then take the square root.

subject: physics
content: Newton's First Law: an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a net force. Second Law: F = m * a, force equals mass times acceleration. Third Law: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

subject: physics
content: Speed is distance travelled over time (a scalar). Velocity is displacement over time, including direction (a vector). Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time: a = (v_final - v_initial) / t.

subject: chemistry
content: An atom has a nucleus containing protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral), surrounded by electrons (negative) in energy levels/shells. The number of protons is the atomic number and defines the element. Electron shells fill in order: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.

subject: chemistry
content: A balanced chemical equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides, per the law of conservation of mass. Balance by adjusting coefficients in front of formulas (never the subscripts within a formula), usually starting with the most complex molecule first.

subject: biology
content: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus (controls the cell), cytoplasm (where reactions happen), and cell membrane (controls what enters/exits). Plant cells additionally have a cell wall, chloroplasts (for photosynthesis), and a large central vacuole.

subject: biology
content: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to convert light energy into chemical energy: carbon dioxide + water, using light energy in the chloroplast, produces glucose and oxygen. The word equation is: carbon dioxide + water --light--> glucose + oxygen.

subject: english
content: A persuasive essay states a clear thesis (your position) and supports it with reasons and evidence, addressing a counterargument to strengthen the case. Structure: introduction with thesis, 2-3 body paragraphs each with one main point and supporting evidence, and a conclusion that restates the thesis in light of the evidence given.

subject: arabic
content: Arabic present-tense verbs (al-mudari) are conjugated by adding a prefix (and sometimes a suffix) to the verb root that matches the subject - for example, a first-person prefix differs from a third-person one. The verb's core meaning stays in its root letters throughout.

subject: french
content: Le comparatif compares two things: plus...que (more...than), moins...que (less...than), aussi...que (as...as) - e.g. 'Elle est plus grande que lui.' Le superlatif expresses an extreme: le/la plus...(the most...) or le/la moins...(the least...) - e.g. 'C'est le plus grand de la classe.'

subject: individuals and societies
content: When evaluating a historical source, consider its origin (who created it and when), purpose (why it was created), and value and limitations (what it can and can't reliably tell us, given who made it and why). A source can be useful even with limitations, as long as those limitations are accounted for.

subject: geography
content: A population pyramid shows the age and gender structure of a population as horizontal bars, youngest at the bottom. A wide base means a high birth rate (common in developing countries); a narrower, more even shape suggests an aging population (common in developed countries).

subject: digital design
content: A low-fidelity prototype (e.g. a paper sketch or simple wireframe) tests an idea's core layout and flow quickly and cheaply, before investing time in a polished version. It should be rough enough to invite feedback and easy changes, while still showing the key elements and how a user would move between them.
